_about: TEST DATA for the browser test, served only by tests/serve.py and labeled as such on screen; the app never serves it. Hand-written answers, not model output, with no timings. conversations.title: AI lecture: LeCun on LLMs (perspectives)
conversations.about: Verbatim Yann LeCun quotes (Lex Fridman Podcast #416, 2024, and a 2023 post on X), played as a lecture.

lines.speaker: Yann LeCun
lines.text: They don't really have persistent memory. They can't really reason and they certainly can't plan.

lines.speaker: Yann LeCun
lines.text: The type of reasoning that takes place in LLM is very, very primitive, and the reason you can tell is primitive is because the amount of computation that is spent per token produced is constant.

lines.speaker: Yann LeCun
lines.text: A house cat has way more common sense and understanding of the world than any LLM.

lines.speaker: Yann LeCun
lines.text: If you're really interested in human level AI, abandon the idea of generative AI.

perspectives.summary: Training on verifiable rewards makes LLMs develop reasoning strategies on their own.
perspectives.quote: By training LLMs against automatically verifiable rewards across a number of environments (e.g. think math/code puzzles), the LLMs spontaneously develop strategies that look like "reasoning" to humans - they learn to break down problem solving into intermediate calculations…

source.title: 2025 LLM Year in Review
source.snippet: By training LLMs against automatically verifiable rewards across a number of environments (e.g. think math/code puzzles), the LLMs spontaneously develop strategies that look like "reasoning" to humans - they learn to break down problem solving into intermediate calculations

perspectives.summary: Agrees they lack memory and continual learning today, but sees about a decade of work, not a dead end.
perspectives.quote: They don't have continual learning. You can't just tell them something and they'll remember it. They're cognitively lacking and it's just not working. It will take about a decade to work through all of those issues.

source.title: Andrej Karpathy — AGI is still a decade away
source.snippet: They don't have continual learning. You can't just tell them something and they'll remember it. They're cognitively lacking and it's just not working. It will take about a decade to work through all of those issues.

perspectives.summary: LLMs imitate what people say; they don't work out what to do.
perspectives.quote: Reinforcement learning is about understanding your world, whereas large language models are about mimicking people, doing what people say you should do. They're not about figuring out what to do.

source.title: Richard Sutton – Father of RL thinks LLMs are a dead end
source.snippet: Reinforcement learning is about understanding your world, whereas large language models are about mimicking people, doing what people say you should do. They're not about figuring out what to do.

perspectives.summary: Ability is jagged: the same models solve hard math and stumble on very dumb problems.
perspectives.quote: The word I came up with to describe the (strange, unintuitive) fact that state of the art LLMs can both perform extremely impressive tasks (e.g. solve complex math problems) while simultaneously struggle with some very dumb problems.

source.title: Jagged Intelligence (post on X)
source.snippet: The word I came up with to describe the (strange, unintuitive) fact that state of the art LLMs can both perform extremely impressive tasks (e.g. solve complex math problems) while simultaneously struggle with some very dumb problems.

perspectives.summary: Weak at silent multistep reasoning, but quite good once allowed to think out loud.
perspectives.quote: I actually think that they are bad at mental multistep reasoning when they are not allowed to think out loud. But when they are allowed to think out loud, they're quite good.

source.title: Ilya Sutskever (OpenAI Chief Scientist) - Building AGI, Alignment, & Future Models
source.snippet: I actually think that they are bad at mental multistep reasoning when they are not allowed to think out loud. But when they are allowed to think out loud, they're quite good.

perspectives.summary: LLMs are a different kind of mind, ghosts rather than animals, so animal yardsticks mislead.
perspectives.quote: Stated plainly, today's frontier LLM research is not about building animals. It is about summoning ghosts.

source.title: Animals vs Ghosts
source.snippet: Stated plainly, today's frontier LLM research is not about building animals. It is about summoning ghosts.

perspectives.summary: Predicting text well requires understanding the reality that produced it.
perspectives.quote: Predicting the next token well means that you understand the underlying reality that led to the creation of that token. It's not statistics. Like it is statistics but what is statistics?

source.title: Ilya Sutskever (OpenAI Chief Scientist) - Building AGI, Alignment, & Future Models
source.snippet: Predicting the next token well means that you understand the underlying reality that led to the creation of that token. It's not statistics. Like it is statistics but what is statistics?

perspectives.summary: LLMs predict what a person would say, not what will happen in the world.
perspectives.quote: A world model would enable you to predict what would happen. They have the ability to predict what a person would say. They don't have the ability to predict what will happen.

source.title: Richard Sutton – Father of RL thinks LLMs are a dead end
source.snippet: A world model would enable you to predict what would happen. They have the ability to predict what a person would say. They don't have the ability to predict what will happen.

perspectives.summary: Language models come first: pretraining supplies the representations everything else builds on.
perspectives.quote: You have to get the language model first, you have to get the representations first, and you have to do that by all the pre-training and all the LLM stuff.

source.title: Andrej Karpathy — AGI is still a decade away
source.snippet: You have to get the language model first, you have to get the representations first, and you have to do that by all the pre-training and all the LLM stuff.

perspectives.summary: Animals don't learn the world from scratch by observation either: they start heavily pre-wired.
perspectives.quote: Animal brains are nowhere near the blank slate they appear to be at birth.

source.title: Animals vs Ghosts
source.snippet: Animal brains are nowhere near the blank slate they appear to be at birth.
